material_risks.finding: Unpromoted requests still become permanently refused on their first budget failure. History begins once the cold zero-credit domain earns only the 100ms start reserve. Moving promotion past all native execution/readback means some otherwise valid requests may fail before the point that permits waiting for future refill.
material_risks.premises: One request starts immediately at the threshold; a single thread consumes approximately one CPU-second per wall-second; no extra idle credit has accumulated. This is a conditional source-derived bound, not a measured native workload.
material_risks.implication: A complete legal relation needing more CPU than this prepromotion envelope may repeatedly fail under immediate retry, even with no malformed traffic. Additional concurrency can reduce available slack further.
material_risks.required_evidence: Run the original cold/depleted honest workload and deadline. Retain failures and HOLD. Do not raise initial credit, extend deadline, bypass accounting or remove full-State qualification just to make a local control pass.
material_risks.agent_response: budget_adversarial acknowledged the limitation and added a separate zero-credit, no-warmup, original 2s cold History honest control. Its small fixture cannot qualify all real inputs.

material_risks.finding: Initial six controls covered plain held, detached, Growth and shared/exclusive History but not the new completion_cpu=Some path in admit_held_prepared. The reviewed add-on now covers that direct original-owner continuation on both backends with invalid/valid/duplicate observations.
material_risks.remaining: The add-on is green-only and explicitly does not exercise dynamic selection above the real snapshot capacity or qualify its latency. Do not describe it as a large-State capacity or original-pressure pass.
